value: 2026-09-10, all on fixtures under the live code at HEAD 57bd9cf. (a) THE SILENCE: a `cairn test --seal --netns` run over a fixture whose standing record was posed at `open` converted it to `sealed` and printed four lines containing neither the word 'override' nor the word 'standing' nor the prior reading — byte-identical in shape to a first seal. (b) THE PERMANENCE: a following plain `cairn test --seal` over the same fixture reproduced `netns`, so the deliberate `open` is gone from the record with nothing saying it ever stood. (c) THE MIRROR ALREADY HOLDS: firing `cairn.tools.base.validation.run_proof(path, sink='validations')` — which never forwards isolation, so it always runs at `none` — over a standing `sealed` raised SealDowngradeRefused, named both readings, offered `unsealing_because`, and left the standing record untouched. (d) THE POPULATION: across both roots, 219 validation trails — 159 standing at `sealed`, 54 at `open`, 6 carrying no seal key at all. All 54 are convertible today by one sweep. (e) `cli.py:379` reads `sink = 'validations' if args.seal else 'none'`, so `--netns` alone persists nothing and only the `--seal` combination reaches the door. (f) Validation records are written 0o444 at rest, which is why a fixture posing a standing seal must chmod and restore. (g) CORRECTED AFTER THE CAST, and it changes the watch: the tester's charter falsifier clause (6) says a validations file holding more than one record is itself a red, and the corpus agrees — all 219 files hold exactly ONE record, and `persist_validation` writes `[record]`. There is no trail and no superseded record. The first cut of this ticket's WATCHME proposed firing when an EARLIER record in a trail carried `open`; that reading is unbuildable because no earlier record exists. The watch is arithmetic against a baseline instead — see the corrected trigger.

The 54 standing `open` readings are NOT re-taken by this ticket. After it ships they still read `open`, and re-taking them becomes an explicit act that must carry a reason — which is the intended shape, not a gap. Their one-time re-take is separate work and is already carried in the queue. Second hole, named: the guard checks that a reason is PRESENT, never that it is a good one. A rote sentence passes. That is deliberate — a sieve measures and does not judge — and it is exactly what the WATCHME below is pointed at, by counting conversions rather than reading reasons.

Item B2 of the build queue, pre-approved by Akien. Cast after measurement corrected its wording: the slate reads 'refuse a downgrade (netns->none) outright', and that half is already physics at validation_store.py:414 — fired and watched to refuse on 2026-09-10. The reachable defect is the mirror direction, open -> measured, which nothing guards. Carrying the slate's wording forward unmeasured would have re-derived a settled answer (Law 1).
